novel_features.name: Guided haircut booking
novel_features.description: Book an appointment end to end — it previews the exact service, staffer, time, and price first, and only sends the real booking when you pass --confirm.
novel_features.rationale: The whole booking funnel (business, service variant, staffer, slot, dry-run validation, confirm) only composes in one place locally; the web app never exposes it as a single scriptable step.
novel_features.why_it_matters: This is the one command that turns 'find me a haircut' into an actual appointment; the dry-run-by-default guard means an agent can plan safely and the human confirms.

novel_features.name: Open slots
novel_features.description: List open time slots for a service at a business over a date range, grouped by day. No login required.
novel_features.rationale: Availability is a POST with a nested subbookings body the web app builds internally; exposing it as clean flags (service variant + date range) is only possible once the funnel is modeled locally.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Lets an agent answer 'when can I get in?' without loading the web calendar — no token needed.

novel_features.name: Services table
novel_features.description: Flatten a business profile into a clean table of bookable services with price, duration, and the service-variant id you pass to book.
novel_features.rationale: Booksy nests services three levels deep (categories -> services -> variants); the variant id needed to book is buried. Flattening it locally is what makes booking one step.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Surfaces the exact --service-variant id an agent needs for availability and booking, with prices to compare.

novel_features.name: Soonest slot
novel_features.description: Find the single earliest open slot for a service across a date window in one call.
novel_features.rationale: Requires scanning the day-grouped time_slots response and returning the first slot — an aggregation no single Booksy endpoint provides.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Answers 'what's the soonest I can get a haircut here?' directly instead of returning a whole calendar.

novel_features.name: Compare barbers
novel_features.description: Compare several businesses side by side on rating, review count, and cheapest matching service price — from the local cache.
novel_features.rationale: Cross-business comparison requires holding multiple business profiles together locally; the API only ever returns one business at a time.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Turns 'which of these barbers is best value?' into one command instead of opening N tabs.

novel_features.name: Cheapest haircut nearby
novel_features.description: Scan search results in a city and rank businesses by the cheapest service matching your query (e.g. haircut), with rating alongside price.
novel_features.rationale: Ranking by service price requires fetching each business's services and joining locally; Booksy's search sorts by score/distance, never by service price.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Answers 'where's the cheapest decent haircut near me?' — a query Booksy's own UI cannot express.

novel_features.name: Cancel appointment
novel_features.description: Cancel one of your Booksy appointments by id — previews the appointment first and only cancels with --confirm.
novel_features.rationale: Completes the booking loop using the appointment _version handshake captured from a real cancellation.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Lets an agent undo a booking it made without opening the Booksy app.

narrative.headline: Book a haircut in Poland from the terminal — search barbers, compare prices and reviews, check open slots, and book, with a dry-run-by-default booking guard.
narrative.value_prop: A CLI over Booksy's Polish marketplace. Public commands (search, business, reviews, suggest) need no login; add BOOKSY_ACCESS_TOKEN for your account and the guided `book` command. `book` previews the exact appointment and only commits with --confirm, so agents can plan safely and you approve the real booking.
narrative.auth_narrative: Public discovery works out of the box. Authenticated actions (your profile, open slots, booking) use your Booksy web session token: copy the `x-access-token` request header value from booksy.com (DevTools -> Network -> any /customer_api/me request) and set it via `booksy-pp-cli auth set-token <token>` or the BOOKSY_ACCESS_TOKEN env var. The public x-api-key and a device fingerprint are built in.

quickstart.comment: Confirm the CLI is wired and reachable (works without a token).
Resolve your city to a location id.
See haircut services and the --service-variant id to book.
Preview the booking; add --confirm to actually book.

troubleshoots.fix: Set your session token: booksy-pp-cli auth set-token <x-access-token from booksy.com>.

troubleshoots.symptom: Search returns nothing for a city name
troubleshoots.fix: Resolve the city first with `discover locations --query <city>` and pass its id via --location-id.

troubleshoots.symptom: book says 'refusing to book under a test harness'
troubleshoots.fix: Expected — book never commits during automated verification; run it interactively with --confirm.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI to search Booksy businesses in Poland, compare barbers/salons on price and rating, check when a service has open slots, and book an appointment from the terminal or an agent. It is the fastest path from 'find me a haircut near X' to a confirmed booking.
anti_triggers: Do not use it for Booksy Biz / provider-side management (staff, calendars, POS) — this is the customer surface only.
Do not use it to bulk-scrape all Booksy businesses; it is built for booking and comparison, not crawling.
Do not use it outside Poland; it is wired to the pl.booksy.com marketplace.
